metas.name: Albania - Bay of Vlore
metas.note: The large Bay of Vlorë can be seen on many parts of the SH4 between Vlorë and Orikum. It can be recognized by the large Karaburun peninsula jutting out into the ocean from the south, and the small Sazan island just to its north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/albania.

metas.name: Albania - Theth National Park
metas.note: The road leading into Theth National Park can typically be recognised by the tall, jagged mountains, often with bare mountainsides.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/albania.

metas.name: Andorra - Autumn Vibes
metas.note: All the Generation 3 coverage was taken in October, meaning that many deciduous trees have autumn colours.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/andorra.

metas.name: Argentina - Buenos Aires Grass Hills
metas.note: Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of Bahía Blanca.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Buenos Aires Lakes
metas.note: Small lakes near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Catamarca Volcanic Rock
metas.note: These volcanic rocks in Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the RP43 south of Antofagasta de la Sierra in northwestern Catamarca.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Central South
metas.note: Flat and barren landscapes like this are typically found in central southern Argentina.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Chaco and Formosa
metas.note: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Cordoba Hills
metas.note:
These mountains are typically found west of Córdoba.

NOTE: They are not as high as the mountains in the west.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Far South
metas.note: If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Grassland
metas.note: Grassland with a few separated tree plantations is generally found in this area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Jujuy Salt Pans
metas.note:
Salt pans in Argentina are typically found in Jujuy.

NOTE: They can also be found in southwestern Bolivia and northeastern Chile, but without Generation 4 coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Misiones Red Soil
metas.note:
Red soil is typically found in the Misiones province.

NOTE: Brazil and Argentina can look similar in this region. Make sure to look for other clues first.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Salta Red Mountains
metas.note: These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - San Luis
metas.note: Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Southern Tierra Del Fuego
metas.note: Beech forests are commonly found in the state of Tierra del Fuego.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Talampaya National Park
metas.note: Red soil with a barren landscape and mountain ranges, can often be seen on the RN76 in Parque Nacional Talampaya in western La Rioja.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Australia - Christmas Island
metas.note: Most of Christmas Island is covered by dense tropical forest. Some unpaved roads feature bright, white sandy soil. A small part of the coverage is in built-up areas. And in some places, palms can be seen.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Coastal Queensland
metas.note: Coastal northern Queensland is very tropical. Typical vegetation consists of palm trees and dark green vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Cocos Islands
metas.note: The general landscape consists of bright white sand, many palms and mowed grass. Cocos Islands is significantly less forested or hilly compared to Christmas Island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Darwin
metas.note: The vegetation in the area surrounding Darwin is extremely distinct. It features dark red soil, as well as rich green grass and trees. The tree trunks are typically black.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Inland New South Wales
metas.note: The landscape in inland NSW is mostly flat, and the soil gets redder the more inland you go. Vegetation consists of mostly dry pale-green shrubs. Further east and on the Queensland and Victorian borders, the climate gets more temperate but is still quite dry and more eucalyptus trees can be seen, with the soil transitioning into a more sandy colour as well as more hills being visible.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Kangaroo Island
metas.note: Kangaroo Island in South Australia tends to have a distinct look. The vegetation mostly consists of bushes and low, stubby eucalyptus trees with puffy clusters of leaves. The orange soil colour is reminiscent of Western Australia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - South Fields
metas.note: Lush green or golden fields can be found in this band from the south of the Yorke Peninsula to Echuca. In the SA side, the landscape should be drier than the Victorian side and more wide crowned eucalyptus can be seen. On the Victorian side, the trees generally have more leaves and are taller.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Southwest South Australia Landscape
metas.note:
The area around Warramboo in SA to Madura in WA has a unique landscape. Vegetation is quite dry and is made up of shrubs and wide crowned eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a slight orange tint. The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has a similar landscape, with the same vegetation but usually with whiter soil.

NOTE: The soil gets more red in the WA side. Redder soil can also be seen more inland on the Victorian side around Mildura.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Tasmania
metas.note:
Tasmania has a cool temperate climate which is uncommon in the rest of Australia and is comparable to central-southern Chile or New Zealand. Typical landscape consists of green rolling hills that can look dry in winter coverage. Eucalyptus trees can be seen on the side of roads and on hills in the distance. Rural Tasmania is also quite hilly with dense eucalyptus forests making up the landscape.

NOTE: Certain areas of Victoria can look similar so make sure to look for other clues.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Tom Price Hills
metas.note: The area around Tom Price can be recognized by its red soil and rocky hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Western Australia
metas.note:
Western Australia, and especially the Perth area, is known for its reddish-orange soil.

NOTE: Although this is very useful, there are numerous areas in WA with light soil, and conversely there are areas in other states with reddish-orange soil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Austria - High Alps
metas.note: The highest parts of the Alps are found in the west and central parts of the country. The tallest mountains are found in the panhandle of Austria, on the Italian border. These mountains can be recognized by their generally sharper peak and grander appearance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/austria.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Eastern Hills
metas.note: While most of Bangladesh is almost completely flat, in the eastern parts of Chittagong you may find fairly tall, forested and uncultivated hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Belgium - Ardennes
metas.note:
The Ardennes, located in the southeast part of Belgium, have a very distinct landscape. You can see a lot of steep hills, dense forests, and valleys.

NOTE: The Ardennes extend partially into France, Luxembourg, and Germany.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/belgium.

metas.name: Belgium - Coastal Plain
metas.note:
The coastal plain is extremely flat and consists of so-called polders, which are man-made fields at or below sea level, surrounded by many waterways. This landscape is situated near the North Sea coast, as well as near the western part of the border with the Netherlands, particularly around Antwerp.

NOTE: This part of Belgium is especially often confused with the Netherlands.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/belgium.

metas.name: Bhutan - Southern Flatlands
metas.note:
Flat landscapes like this in Bhutan can only be found in the south.

NOTE: The coverage in the south is limited to the four regions shown on the map.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bhutan.

metas.name: Bhutan - Vibes
metas.note:
Bhutan is a mountainous country and most of the coverage is located on its main mountain roads.

NOTE: In the south are flat areas where you cannot see any mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bhutan.

metas.name: Bolivia - Chile Border Desert
metas.note: Between the villages of Villa Catalina and Coipasa, there is an isolated stretch of coverage where the Google car drove through extremely arid desert terrain. This small road is located close to the southwestern end of Ruta 12, near the Chilean border. It can be hard to spot on the map, because it blends in with the salt flat. Closer to Villa Catalina, the car drove over the salt flat. Closer to Coipasa, the car drove on an unpaved dirt road, where you can see cone-shaped volcanic hills. In both parts, there is virtually no vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Bolivia - Lake Titicaca
metas.note: Lake Titicaca, on the border with Peru, is the most significant body of water in Bolivia. It is located entirely within the Altiplano. The landscape around Titicaca is very green, compared to most of the western half of Bolivia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Bolivia - Northern Altiplano
metas.note:
The grasslands of the Altiplano tend to look more lush in the more northern half: the area close to El Alto and La Paz.

NOTE: Due to seasonal coverage, there are some exceptions to this, but in general this is a good rule of thumb to distinguish between the different parts of the Altiplano.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Bolivia - Sajama National Park
metas.note: Sajama National Park was covered by this unique Google car: it has a black roof rack with a series of metal bars. The coverage is on an unpaved road surrounded by fluffy bushes. The Nevado Sajama volcano is always visible. The car briefly drove through the small village of Tomarapi, which can be recognized by its traditional buildings with adobe walls and thatched roofs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Bolivia - Santa Cruz Area
metas.note: Within the tropical area of Bolivia, coverage on unpaved roads is only found around Santa Cruz. These roads again prominently have the pink soil that is very characteristic of the area east of Andes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Bolivia - Southern Altiplano
metas.note:
The Altiplano looks more arid in the more southern half: around Oruro, and the roads going southwest towards Chile.

NOTE: There is one major exception to this: one driving side of the divided part of Ruta 1 looks somewhat green all the way up to Oruro (due to this coverage being captured in a different season).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Bolivia - Wider Santa Cruz Area
metas.note: The area east of the Andes is very green and tropical, with lots of agriculture – especially around Santa Cruz. This area is mostly very flat, though you will see large hills on some of the roads closer to the Andes. The soil tends to have a pink colour.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Botswana - Eastern Hills
metas.note:
Most of Botswana is as flat as a pancake. However, every now and then you will find some elevation. If you see hills, you are most likely in one of the two areas indicated on the minimap.

NOTE: Even in the indicated areas, there are a lot of very flat areas, as many of Botswana’s hills are geographically isolated. Some lone hills may also appear far outside the indicated areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Francistown Area
metas.note: The landscape in the eastern pocket north of Francistown is characterised by red soil and a somewhat arid look. The soil in these two areas often looks firm and rocky, rather than sandy or dusty. Trees and bushes with yellowed leaves and other “autumn” colours are common. Many trees are bare and withered. You might see fallen leaves on the ground here and there.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Gaborone Hills
metas.note:
The southeastern region near Gaborone has many semi-arid hills covered in short shrubs. If you see a lot of these, you are likely to be in the area between Gaborone and Lobatse.

NOTE: Similar hills can be found elsewhere in the country and across the border in South Africa. If you see a large quantity of them, and use other clues to rule out South Africa, you can be fairly certain that you are in southeastern Botswana.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Salt Pans
metas.note:
Salt pans can be found in central-eastern Botswana. Dirt road coverage can be found leading to the pans and has similar soil and grass, but you can also find many trees along the road. They are mainly found around the Nwetwe pan. The salt pans show up as lakes on the map.

NOTE: A lot of the dirt road coverage near the pans was taken in June, and will feature trees without leaves or those that are beginning to lose their leaves.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Tsodilo Hills
metas.note: The Tsodilo Hills World Heritage Site is memorable due to its large protruding hills with exposed rock faces. The coverage around the hills is entirely on dirt roads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - White Soil
metas.note:
A large region in the middle western part of the country is characterised by very white sandy soil. In addition, the vegetation tends to look very dry.

NOTE: Sandy soil can be found in many places in Botswana. This tip specifically refers to the bright white colour of the sand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Brazil - Acre
metas.note: Acre has a unique landscape of small grass hills and sparsely growing trees. The roads often do not cut around the hills like in most of Brazil, but ride the hills instead. A similar landscape can also be seen near Maraba in the state of Pará.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Coastal Rio Grande do Sul
metas.note: Coastal regions in Rio Grande do Sul are recognisable due to being a rare flat wetland, which is uncommon in Brazil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - North Roraima Mountains
metas.note: The landscape near the town of Uiramuta, in northern Roraima, features a very distinct landscape. It is dry, with large mountains containing numerous “folds.”
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Northeast Landscape
metas.note: Northeastern Brazil can be identified by its dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga landscape). In rainy season coverage, the shrubs are still recognisable, but can be deceptively green.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Rio Grande do Sul
metas.note: The landscape in Rio Grande do Sul can be hilly or flat with lush, green fields. Southern areas can have some resemblance to Uruguay.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Rocky Mountains
metas.note: Espírito Santo, and the surrounding areas, often have large mountains with exposed rock.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Roraima Plains
metas.note: Rural locations in Roraima are mostly open grassy plains with large, distant mountains in the background. Occasionally, you are on roads within the mountains. Furthermore, the grass in Roraima is distinctly thin, and grows in bunches.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Southeast Rolling Hills
metas.note: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo often have rolling grassy hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Tocantins Grass
metas.note: Very tall grass can be often seen in the centre of the country, most notably in the Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Cambodia - Central Plain
metas.note: The low-lying central plain is home to most agricultural land. The landscape is flat, cultivated, and dotted with villages and farms.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Cambodia - Northeast
metas.note: Conversely, the northeast is much more uncultivated: there is less agriculture and more natural vegetation. Some areas are slightly hilly.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Cambodia - Northern Ridge
metas.note: Near the northern border with Thailand, you can often see a mountainous ridgeline to your north. The soil in this region tends to be red, ranging from a slight reddish tinge to deep dark red.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Cambodia - Southeast Light Soil
metas.note: Sandy, white soil is very common in the region southeast of Phnom Penh, as well as around the city itself. The colour can range from bright white to slightly beige.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Cambodia - Southwest Mountains
metas.note: The southwest is the area with the most elevation in Cambodia. This region is characterized by hills and low mountains. Some inland roads feature dense forest cover, but the coastal areas in particular are fairly densely populated.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Canada - Cape Breton National Park
metas.note: The Cape Breton Highlands in northeastern Nova Scotia have an unusual amount of elevation for Eastern Canadian standards. It is very forested, with a mix of broad-leaf trees and pine trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Drumheller Canyons
metas.note: The area near Drumheller, Alberta has distinct canyon-like treeless rock formations that comprise the landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Gaspé Peninsula
metas.note: The inland roads of the Gaspé Peninsula feature densely forested mountainous terrain. It is particularly common to encounter overcast coverage in this region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Great Plains
metas.note: The Great Plains are mostly flat, with some rolling hills. There is a lot of agriculture, very few trees, and it is very sparsely populated. The landscape gets drier the further south-southwest you go, with the driest parts near the border with the US state of Montana.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Max Max North Coverage
metas.note:
The northernmost Google Street View coverage in the world is a trekker on Ellesmere Island in northern Nunavut. It shows a glacier in a rocky, desolate landscape that is devoid of any vegetation.

NOTE: This coverage is sometimes used in maps to improve and standardise the scoring range. As a result, you might encounter this trekker in competitive maps like ACW, despite it not being pinpointable.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Québec City Windsor Corridor
metas.note:
The Québec City-Windsor Corridor is the most densely populated part of Canada. It is mostly flat and green, with a patchwork of agriculture and occasional forest cover.

NOTE: This area can look similar to the Great Lakes region in the US.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - South Saskatchewan Hills
metas.note:
Southern Saskatchewan has many river valleys, which means that the province can have a barren hilly landscape; much more so than the rest of the Canadian Great Plains, which tends to be really flat.

NOTE: Some of this hilliness extends into southern Alberta and Manitoba.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Southern British Columbia
metas.note: The landscape in the interior of southern British Columbia, mostly centred around the towns of Kamloops and Kelowna, has a distinct look. It is generally hilly and a little more arid than the rest of BC, The vegetation consists of sprawling brown grasslands, and pine tree forests on the hillsides.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Western Mountains
metas.note: Western Canada is very mountainous. The highest mountains are in British Columbia, western Alberta, and parts of Yukon. Outside these provinces, large mountains are rare to non-existent in Canada.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Yukon
metas.note: Yukon has a very northern, boreal landscape that is mostly hilly, sometimes with large mountains in the distance. Coniferous trees line the roads and the further north you go, the thinner and shorter the trees get. While this region recently got a lot of new Generation 4, older Generation 2 coverage is still very common.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Chile - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve
metas.note:
A vast, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and high altitude feel. Monkey puzzles are also seen toward the east.

NOTE: Ruta 181 leading up to the reserve also has triple yellow lines, however, is less vast with more vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Alto Loa National Reserve
metas.note: Alto Loa National Reserve can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to snow-capped volcanoes. The reserve does not have any paved roads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Arica Sandy Mountains
metas.note: The province of Arica y Parinacota can be recognized by the smooth, sandy mountains that may look slightly eroded, or have bulbous formations. Valleys are also common, which are rarely seen in other parts of Chile.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Atacama Mountains
metas.note: These rocky, uneven mountains are most commonly seen in Atacama and northern Coquimbo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Aysen Autumn
metas.note: Southern Aysén can be recognised by autumn coverage, having orange and red coloured vegetation. Keep in mind that not all coverage in this region will have fall colours.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Isla Grande de Chiloe
metas.note:
A rolling, agricultural landscape, comparable to New Zealand, can be seen on Isla Grande de Chiloé.

NOTE: Similar looking landscapes exist in some other parts of the country, but usually more level.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Lauca National Park
metas.note: A distinct landscape consisting of a line of snow-capped mountains with two other isolated, symmetrical snow-capped volcanoes are seen in Lauca National Park. Most of the roads are newly paved and have a smooth, dark look.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Llanos des Challe National Park
metas.note:
Llanos de Challe National Park can be recognized by the brown coloured dirt on the roadside, patches of light sand, juniper plants, and dark coloured mountains. The sky is overcast in most of the coverage.

NOTE: Pan de Azúcar National Park looks similar, however has less vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Los Flamencos National Reserve
metas.note: Smooth mountains with a reddish tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines, with short dashes in the west.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Lush Mountain Valleys
metas.note: Lush green valleys, with rocky mountains and often overcast coverage, can be seen in southern Los Lagos and northern Aysén.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Maule
metas.note: Compared to the area around Santiago, the Maule province has a similar look. However, it has a Mediterranean climate, and is generally greener. Vineyards are also commonly seen in this region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Nevado des Cruzes National Park
metas.note: In the west, Nevado Tres Cruces National Park can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to a line of mountains. The sand has a reddish tint. In the east, the Google Car drives up a mountain pass with views of lightly snow-capped volcanoes and snow on the side of the road. The roads in the National Park are paved in newer coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Puyehue National Park
metas.note: Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and tar snakes are frequently seen. In the east, many dead trees can be seen with a lack of leaves.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Santiago Landscape
metas.note: The region around Santiago can be recognized by its semi-arid climate, having dry hills and scattered vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Colombia - Colombia North
metas.note: The Northern part of the country is characterised by white, sandy soil and an arid landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/colombia.

metas.name: Colombia - East of Andes Lowlands
metas.note: East of the Andes lies a vast lowland called Llanos. It is characterised by open tropical grasslands, savannas with scattered trees, small areas of forest and seasonal flooding.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/colombia.

metas.name: Colombia - La Guajira
metas.note: This landscape is typical of the far Northern province of La Guajira: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti. In addition, you can often recognise the Uribia-Puerto Bolivar road because of this landscape, the straightness and the train track always present to the East.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/colombia.

metas.name: Croatia - Adriatic Coast
metas.note: The Adriatic coast features rocky mountains similar to those seen in Montenegro or Albania. Shrubs are more common instead of trees along the coast, especially in the south. This coastal region has a lot of islands and peninsulas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Croatia - Agricultural Hills
metas.note: The region north and west of Zagreb is hilly and agricultural.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Croatia - East Flatland
metas.note: The north-eastern region of Croatia is mostly flat and features a lot of agriculture. It is similar in terms of landscape to Hungary and north-western Serbia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Croatia - Istria
metas.note: The north-western region of Istria, south of the Italian city of Trieste, sometimes has distinct red soil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Curacao - General Landscape
metas.note: Rural Curaçao is characterised by a semi-arid rural landscape with green, but dry hills. Houses are spread apart, with the roads in the west quite narrow in width.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/curacao.

metas.name: Czechia - North Hills
metas.note:
Much of the northern Bohemian landscape can be characterised by a rolling landscape combined with steep solitary hills.

NOTE: The hills can sometimes have castles on the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Rolling Hills
metas.note: The Czech landscape is fairly rolling, with a lot of hills and altitude changes, but not a lot of tall mountains. Generally speaking, Slovakia has more mountains, but also more completely flat areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Denmark - Faroer Island Vibes
metas.note: The landscape of the Faroe islands is characterised by long, wide fjords with jagged green mountains that rise straight out of the water, with rocky ridge lines along the mountainsides. The mountains generally look more imposing and greener than coastal mountains in Iceland, which can often be used to tell them apart.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/denmark.

metas.name: Dominican Republic - Santo Domingo Outskirts
metas.note: This type of landscape is found on the outskirts of Santo Domingo. It is characterised by narrow dirt tracks, whitish dirt, dried green shrubbery and debris next to the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic.

metas.name: Ecuador - Chimborazo
metas.note: The province of Chimborazo is semi-arid, and has an abundance of pine trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Ecuador - Ecuador Amazon
metas.note: The Amazon area is very distinct. It is fairly flat, and contains many of these trees with white bark (Cordia trichotoma), and oil palms. The vast majority of the coverage notably uses the rarer “high antenna”.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Ecuador - Ecuador Dry Coast
metas.note: This extremely dry landscape is only found in the coastal region between Guayaquil and Manta.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Ecuador - Esmeraldas Landscape
metas.note: The province of Esmeraldas can look similar to the Amazon region, but it is significantly hillier.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Ecuador - Galapagos Islands
metas.note: The Galapagos Islands are an archipelago located west of mainland Ecuador. There are only trekkers and boat coverage on and around the islands. There is a wide variety of landscapes, including volcanic soil, low shrubbery, and craters.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Ecuador - Guayaquil Flatland
metas.note: The flattest region is located around the city of Guayaquil. This is most easily seen on the E-25 and E-48. The Amazon area is also very flat, and will be described below.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Ecuador - Southern Mountains
metas.note: The southern regions have many winding mountain roads and exposed brownish red dirt. The central provinces can have similar roads, but the exposed dirt will usually not be found in these areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Eswatini - Central South Mountains
metas.note:
This distinct region in the central South of the country, mostly along the MR9, can be recognized by the dark, overwhelming greenness and tall wooded mountains.

NOTE: If you are struggling to see why this is unique, try comparing this to other areas of the country, which are more “golden” and light-coloured.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/eswatini.

metas.name: Eswatini - Eastern Flatland
metas.note: You can recognise this region in the east of the country thanks to the unusual flatness and the mountains often visible in the distance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/eswatini.

metas.name: Eswatini - Grassland
metas.note:
Montane grasslands with long golden grass and a mountainous landscape are typical of Western Eswatini.

NOTE: Long grass can be found in almost all areas of Eswatini. This clue refers specifically to the pristine golden colour most commonly seen in the Western highlands.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/eswatini.

metas.name: Germany - Alps
metas.note: The German Alps is the most mountainous region in Germany, it is mostly concentrated on the Austrian Border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Germany - Sylt
metas.note:
The shrub and sand covered hills are unique to the island of Sylt. And like the rest of the North Frisian Islands, rock walls, brick houses, and thatched roofs are common.

NOTE: Some parts of Sylt look more generic, but still very flat.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Ghana - East of Accra Landscape
metas.note: The coastal area just east of Accra, especially on the N1, has a distinct landscape: it is very flat and wide open, with significantly less vegetation than the rest of southern Ghana. Some parts can look somewhat dry.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - Eastern Mountains
metas.note:
Tall mountain ranges in Ghana are typically seen near Lake Volta in the highlighted area.

NOTE: Mountain ranges to the east are more common in the area near Togo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - North Savannah
metas.note: Northern Ghana features a savannah landscape, which can be identified by its dry soil and less dense vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - Rainforest
metas.note: Dense forests in Ghana are typically found in the southwest and east. You will usually see many naturally occurring palm trees, making the two regions recognizable.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - Wa Roads
metas.note:
Most unpaved roads in a dry savannah landscape are found north of Wa, as well as near the town itself.

NOTE: The other unpaved roads in northern Ghana are the Yendi-Nkwanta road in the east, and part of the Salaga-Tamale road, which has very distinct soil. See the tips below.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Greece - Barren Islands
metas.note: On many of the central islands you can find a very barren landscape, with small bushes and no trees in sight. This tends to be more common on the smaller islands with coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Greece - Flat Valleys
metas.note: The largest flat agricultural valleys in Greece are found close to Thessaloniki and Larissa, but smaller flat valleys, where the mountains generally appear closer, can be found in several other areas in the north and centre of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Greece - Mount Pangaion
metas.note: Mount Pangaion can be recognised from its shape, being more of a solitary mountain rather than a wide mountain range, combined with the fact that it is located to the south of a flat agricultural valley.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Greece - Tall Mountains
metas.note: The tallest Greek mountains are found in the western half of the country, and contain most of the country’s high-altitude mountain roads with coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Guatemala - Lago de Atitlán
metas.note: Lago de Atitlán is by far the largest lake in the mountainous regions of Guatemala. It is surrounded by mountains, and some volcanoes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/guatemala.

metas.name: Guatemala - Mountains
metas.note: The central regions of Guatemala are generally mountainous.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/guatemala.

metas.name: Guatemala - North
metas.note: The northern regions of Guatemala are typically fairly flat. You will however usually see some hills or a slightly rolling landscape, rather than the complete flatness of the south.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/guatemala.

metas.name: Guatemala - South
metas.note: The southern regions of Guatemala mainly consist of completely flat agricultural land. It is generally more built up than flat areas in the north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/guatemala.

metas.name: Hungary - Mountains
metas.note: While the southeastern parts of Hungary are extremely flat, with almost no noticeable hills, the northern and western parts mainly consist of forested hills and mountains. The tallest mountains are found in the north, while the southwestern mountains are generally slightly lower.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/hungary.

metas.name: Hungary - Puszta Grasslands
metas.note: Unlike most of the Hungarian plains, which is almost entirely cultivated land, the Puszta, centred around Hortobágy National Park, mainly consists of barren and wet, natural grasslands.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/hungary.

metas.name: Iceland - Barren Volcanic Landscape
metas.note: Barren landscapes consisting mostly of dark volcanic gravel, with little to no vegetation or signs of life, are typical of the inland regions of Iceland. Most such covered roads are located in the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: Iceland - Eastfjords
metas.note: The far east of the country is home to several fjords similar to the Westfjords. What distinguishes them are the generally larger and more jagged mountains in the East.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: Iceland - Eiðar Valley
metas.note: The wide valley around Eiðar is slightly hilly and agricultural, with tall, snowy peaks visible in the distance on either side, to the east and northwest, respectively.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: Iceland - Farmland
metas.note:
The Southwest agricultural area in Iceland can be identified by its relatively flat farmland landscape scattered with numerous farmsteads, fields, meadows and grasslands.

NOTE: Although there are other smaller agricultural areas in Iceland, mountains in this area tend to be quite distant, making it unique.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: Iceland - Glaciers
metas.note: The southern coast of Iceland features some impressive glaciers visible from the ring road, spilling into the sea from the Vatnajökull ice cap.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: Iceland - Selfoss Mountain
metas.note: You can recognise the area near the town of Selfoss from its distinct flat-ridge mountain. Due to the otherwise flat landscape, this mountain can be seen from a wide area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: Iceland - Westfjords
metas.note:
Iceland often looks barren and treeless. Most regions have a dark grey soil consisting mostly of volcanic rocks.

NOTE: Due to the lack of trees, the landscape in Iceland does not look like anywhere else in Northern Europe.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: India - Ganges Valley
metas.note: The northern plains, also known as the Ganges River Valley, of India are very fertile with extremely flat and open agricultural fields.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: India - Gujarat Salt Flats
metas.note:
Salt flats and coastal marshes with nearly no vegetation, other than short yellow or brown grass, can be found in parts of Gujarat. Shallow bodies of water can often be seen around these areas.

NOTE: The soil in western Rajasthan will be a lot more sandy and you’ll typically be able to see short desert shrubs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: India - Himalayas
metas.note: The by far tallest mountains in India are found in the Himalayas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: India - Ladakh
metas.note: In Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh you can find an extremely dry landscape with little to no vegetation within the Himalayan mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: India - Maharashtra Soil
metas.note: Distinctly dark soil is mainly found in Maharashtra and adjacent regions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: India - Mizoram Mountains
metas.note:
The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded hillsides having many small peaks scattered around.

NOTE: A somewhat similar landscape can be found in Meghalaya, however rather than distinct peaks, the hillsides will have a mostly smooth and flat top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: India - West Ghats
metas.note:
The Western Ghats Mountains in the western part of Maharashtra can be recognised by their distinct ridgelines, often having plateaus rather than peaks. The northern part is drier while the southern part has more vegetation.

NOTE: During the rainy season the mountains will turn green and appear quite different.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: India - West Rajasthan
metas.note: The western parts of Rajasthan can commonly be recognised by the dry landscape with sandy soil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: Indonesia - Lake Toba
metas.note: The region around Lake Toba, in North Sumatra, can be recognized by mountains surrounding the lake and Samosir Island in the middle. Overcast coverage is also common for the region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/indonesia.

metas.name: Indonesia - Nusa Islands
metas.note:
The Nusas typically look drier than other regions in Indonesia. The islands get especially dry towards the east, especially in Generation 3. Vegetation tends to look less tropical, but instead more brown with a lack of leaves. Sumba Island is also the driest of the Nusas.

NOTE: While less common, other regions such as Java can look similarly dry. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/indonesia.

metas.name: Indonesia - Palu Bay
metas.note: Palu Bay is a unique slightly north-west facing bay just north of Palu city, which features mountains to the west of the bay, and a flat, more urbanised landscape to the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/indonesia.

metas.name: Indonesia - Red Soil
metas.note: Red soil can often be found on Batam and the Banga Belitung islands, located east of mainland Sumatra.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/indonesia.

metas.name: Ireland - Burren National Park
metas.note: The area in and around Burren National Park is characterised by a unique karst landscape consisting of exposed grey limestone rocks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ireland.

metas.name: Ireland - Donegal
metas.note: If a very small rural road has Generation 4 coverage and is located in an unusually hilly landscape, you are likely to be in Donegal. Note that this meta only applies to the smallest roads: thin, without road lines, and sometimes with grass in the middle. This type of coverage is also not exclusive to Donegal, it is just likely to be there.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ireland.

metas.name: Ireland - Tabletop Mountains
metas.note: In the north of counties Sligo and Leitrim you can find distinctive tabletop mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ireland.

metas.name: Ireland - Western Mountains
metas.note: Ireland’s west coast is defined by a rugged, hilly landscape. Steep hills and low mountains dominate. The neat fields of the east make way for wild grass- and moorlands. The grass often has more brownish and yellow tones to it. Sometimes you will be able to see exposed rocks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ireland.

metas.name: Ireland - Wicklow Mountains
metas.note: One noteworthy area in the east is the Wicklow Mountains, just south of Dublin. They can look deceptively similar to the western coastal mountains. It can be very hard, if not downright impossible to distinguish these two areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ireland.

metas.name: Israel - Eilat Mountains
metas.note: These tall, rocky mountains can be found east of Eilat, making the city very easy to recognize.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Jerusalem Hills
metas.note: The area west of Jerusalem can often look deceptively similar to northern Israel, with green forested hills and some agriculture sprinkled across the landscape. Two things can occasionally be used to tell the two apart. Firstly, in northern Israel you may occasionally see wide, flat valleys, while the Jerusalem area is always going to be hilly. Secondly, if you see houses made of Jerusalem stone, you are likely to be near Jerusalem.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Mount Carmel
metas.note: Mount Carmel is a long mountain ridge, going northwest to southeast, near the city of Haifa. From the northeast, it can easily be recognised by its direction and size. There is also a lot of coverage on top of the mountain range, which is generally fairly green and looks noticeably high altitude.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Mount Gilboa
metas.note: Mount Gilboa is a very dry looking mountain, which can be seen from far away and from many angles. There is some coverage on top of the mountain, which is very green and often with a very good view over the surrounding valleys.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Mount Tavor
metas.note: Mount Tavor is located in the Northern District and can be recognised by its soft, round shape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - North
metas.note: Northern Israel is usually far more mountainous and green than the rest of Israel. Throughout the region you will almost always see forested hills and mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Southern Dryness
metas.note: Southern Israel and eastern West Bank are extremely dry and sandy.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - Timna National Park
metas.note: Timna National park can be recognised by the complete dryness combined with the mountain ridges in all directions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Israel - West Bank
metas.note: Most of the West Bank has a semi-arid Mediterranean landscape. It is generally greener than southern Israel, drier than northern Israel and west of Jerusalem, and hillier and less agricultural than central Israel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Italy - Alps
metas.note: The alpine region in northern Italy has tall, wide mountain ranges and deep valleys.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Italy - Etna
metas.note: Etna, the tallest volcano in Europe, can be seen rising above the landscape from far away in eastern Sicily.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Italy - Po Valley
metas.note: The Padan Plain (commonly referred to as Po Valley) can typically be recognized by its complete flatness. The plain has some of the worst air quality in Europe, which has led to much of the coverage having a noticeable haze.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Italy - Salina
metas.note: Within the Aeolian islands, Salina can easily be distinguished from the twin volcanoes forming a valley across the island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Italy - Sardinia
metas.note:
Grey rocks sticking up from the ground are commonly found on Sardinia, particularly in the northeast.

NOTE: A similar phenomenon can be seen on Sicily, however the landscape will typically be much drier than Sardinia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Italy - Sicily
metas.note: The Sicilian landscape is characterised by an arid, hilly agricultural landscape, often combined with rocky mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Italy - Vesuvius
metas.note: The volcano of Vesuvius can often be seen to the south or east from the plains around Naples.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Italy - Vulcano
metas.note: Vulcano is perhaps the most easily recognisable of the Aeolian islands, with its volcano having an almost white stripe of dirt following the top of the mountainside. It can typically be spotted from afar on the island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Jordan - Madaba Fields
metas.note:
Near and in the city of Madaba, you will find flat fields which are sometimes tilled. They uniquely have the characteristic of rich, red soil.

NOTE: The fields continue both north and south of Madaba, along Highway 35.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/jordan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Autumn Hills
metas.note: The East Kazakhstan Region is hilly and forested. It was covered in october, so you will see fall colours on the vegetation. The town of Ridder itself is flat, but surrounded by hazy mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Birch Forests
metas.note:
These lush birch forests next to green fields are common in northern Kazakhstan.

NOTE: This landscape often appears very similar to that found in and around Omsk Oblast in Russia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Desert Landscape
metas.note: Sandy and shrubby desert-like landscapes are common in southwestern Kazakhstan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Grassy Rolling Hills
metas.note: Grassy green rolling hills can be found in southern Kazakhstan. They are especially common just north of Bishkek
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Green Plains
metas.note: Vast grassy green plains are found in northwestern Kazakhstan. They are especially common in Akmola and Kostanay regions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Tall Mountains
metas.note: Tall mountains, which are often snow-capped, can be seen in southeastern Kazakhstan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Uzbek Border
metas.note:
The landscape in southern Kazakhstan near Uzbekistan is hilly and quite dry and shrubby, with a lot of orange looking grass. The landscape consists of dry but grassy rolling hills or dead flat agricultural land near Zhetisay.

NOTE: These red and white KM markers that look like Kyrgyz ones, are only found near Zhetisay.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kenya - Amboseli National Park
metas.note: Amboseli National Park has a grey car with a small snorkel. It is very flat with tan grass, few trees, and dried up lake beds. You can always see the base of Kilimanjaro to the south, with most of it obscured by clouds.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Far West
metas.note: The far west areas of the country that are northwest and southwest of Kisumu are the most agricultural parts of the country. You will often see farms, grassy hills, and tall eucalyptus trees in this region of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Kerio Lodwar Region
metas.note: The area surrounding and between Kerio and Lodwar uses the same car as the Aberdare National Park, but with a vastly different landscape. It is very sandy, dry, and has little vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Kitui
metas.note: The area around Kitui is semi-arid, usually mountainous, and has light orange, sandy dirt.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Mara Triangle
metas.note: Mara Triangle has no considerable mountains and most of it is either flat or hilly. It has a white car that can be found in other Kenyan National Parks. Most of the coverage is not within the park, but to the east of it.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Northwest
metas.note: The northwest part of the country has very limited coverage, most of which is on the A1 or in Sibiloi National Park. It has faintly tan soil and sparse low trees. A lot of the coverage in this area is very flat, but you can also see hills or mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Lesotho - Mountains
metas.note: Conversely, in the mountainous part, the road will usually be directly on the side of the mountain, instead of slightly away from it. The mountains are often large, closer to the road, and covered in green grass. Coverage in the mountainous part of Lesotho is very sparse: there are only 6 main roads (and a couple of very small off-roads) with coverage, meaning that you can learn each road by heart if you feel so inclined.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Lesotho - Western Flatness
metas.note: Lesotho can be roughly divided into two regions, based on landscape: flat and mountainous. In the flat region, the road itself runs through a mostly flat or hilly landscape. “Flat” is a bit of a misnomer, as you will usually still see tabletop-like mountains around you. However they will usually be significantly further away from the road, giving you a more clear line of sight. This “flat” part is the region with the most coverage, settlements and agriculture.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Malaysia - Perlis Rocks
metas.note: These isolated rock formations, rising abruptly from an otherwise flat landscape, can be found near the Thai border in Perlis state.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malaysia - Sabah Mountains
metas.note:
Assuming you are on Borneo: the state of Sabah is very mountainous, and much of the coverage is on mountain roads like this one.

NOTE: Sarawak generally has flatter roads. Even if you see mountains, they will usually be at a distance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malta - Vibes
metas.note: The general landscape of Malta consists of slightly hilly dry agricultural fields. Many roads are also only 1 or 2 lanes wide, due to the island’s size. Having a mediterranean climate, cacti and various dry shrubs can be seen.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malta.

metas.name: Mexico - Campeche Fields
metas.note: These red agricultural fields surrounded by dense forests of tropical trees are most common in northern Campeche.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Cerro Del Bernal
metas.note: Cerro del Bernal is a distinct extinct volcano that is found in southern Tamaulipas. It can be found heading directly northwest of Tampico or west of Morón.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Ciudad Juárez Outskirts
metas.note: The outskirts of Ciudad Juárez features a lot of dirt roads with a distinct shade of orange soil and low shrubs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Guanajuato Dark Fields
metas.note: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Guaymas Mountains
metas.note: The town of Guaymas has a lot of jagged cliffs and mountains that make the area very distinct. The soil is also distinctly pinkish and organ-pipe cacti can be seen scattered on the hills and next to the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Los Coloradas Pink Lakes
metas.note: The town of Los Coloradas is famously known for the pink lakes around the area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Maderas del Carmen Biosphere Reserve Ridge
metas.note: This tall, flat ridge, with very prominent ridgelines, belongs to the Maderas del Carmen Biosphere Reserve in Northern Coahuila near the US border. NOTE: The only road the mountain range can be observed from is the Federal Highway 53 that leads to Boquillas del Carmen.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Mexicali Farmland
metas.note: The area around Mexicali features flat farmland with a ridge to the west. Washingtonia palms are very common and these poles made out of brown wood can be found.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Monterrey Mountains
metas.note: The Monterrey metropolitan area features tall stunning mountain ranges that surround the city.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - North Baja California Hills
metas.note: These reddish brown-tinged hills, often accompanied by large boulders, are a common sight for the northern half of Baja California.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Rocky Mountains
metas.note: The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with pine forests. In general, these pines are shorter and more stunted in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca Hills
metas.note: The area around San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca and south of it in Oaxaca often feature rolling hills with really distinct orange and beige-tinged soil, passing from one colour to the other with each hill. The beige-tinged soil can be seen more prominent in some locations.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve
metas.note: This extremely long and flat ridge is found in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve in eastern San Luis Potosi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Twin Volcanoes
metas.note: The twin volcanoes of Iztaccíhuatl and Popocatépetl are found on the border between the State of Mexico and Puebla. Keep in mind that they are usually much less visible than depicted in the image, which is just for reference.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Zacatecas Red Fields
metas.note: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mongolia - Bugant Forest
metas.note: Around the town of Bugant is a large forest that stands out for having narrow dirt trails with close trees, typically on both sides, in a way that can appear quite Russian. Additionally, it is very common to see birches around this area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Eastern Grass Fields
metas.note: Small dirt tracks within flat, vast grassy fields are mainly found in far eastern Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Far West Peaks
metas.note: In the westmost part of Mongolia, there is some very remote coverage showcasing the tallest mountains in Mongolia where you can see glaciers and snow-capped peaks. This area also has a unique Street View car with a green or black bag above the right side roof racks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Gobi Gurvan Saikhan National Park
metas.note: The Gobi Gurvan Saikhan National Park, in the far south of Mongolia, features bright orange sand and sand dunes. There are two separate spots covered in the park: one in the middle just north of Sevrei, which has distant southern mountains, and the other in the far southwest corner of the park, which has a Jeep follow car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Khan Khokhii National Park
metas.note:
Khan Khokhii is a national park in northwestern Mongolia with some of the most dense forests in the country. It has partially cloudy skies, dark soil, and the western grey tent. Keep in mind that the trails in this park do not appear on the map.

NOTE: There are other forests in Mongolia, but Khan Khokhii is one of the biggest and one of the only areas where you can be completely surrounded by trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Mongolia Forests
metas.note: You can find forests, typically surrounded by grassy fields, all around northern Mongolia. Generally these will be Siberian Larches, with pines and birches being common as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Southwestern Steppe
metas.note: You can find arid steppe rangeland, characterised by the coarse soil, patchy grass, and small shrubs, throughout southwestern Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - West Mountains
metas.note: These dry, rugged hills and mountains are common to see in far western Mongolia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Montenegro - Dry Mountains
metas.note: Dry mountains with a lack of trees are seen around Podgorica, and to the south of it. Vineyards are also commonly seen in this region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/montenegro.

metas.name: Montenegro - Durmitor National Park
metas.note: Durmitor National Park can be recognized by a distinct landscape consisting of grassy, treeless mountains with a high-altitude feel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/montenegro.

metas.name: Montenegro - Northern Agricultural Valleys
metas.note: Green, agricultural valleys with deforested hills to make way for farmland are most commonly seen in the north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/montenegro.

metas.name: Netherlands - Dunes
metas.note: Most of the Dutch North Sea coast is lined by dunes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/netherlands.

metas.name: Netherlands - Flevoland
metas.note: Almost all of the land belonging to the province of Flevoland was reclaimed from the sea in the mid-20th century. As a result, the province has a distinct, man-made look: extremely straight roads and large crop fields dominate the landscape. Wind turbines are common.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/netherlands.

metas.name: Netherlands - Polder
metas.note: Most of the west and north is at or below sea-level. As a result, most of this region’s countryside has a distinct “polder” landscape: the landscape is marshy, often with a large amount of small waterways.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/netherlands.

metas.name: New Zealand - Cold Flatlands
metas.note: The flatter parts of the Southland and Otago regions can be recognised by their cold climate and sloping, alpine hills. The vegetation in this area is often quite stunted due to the climate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Glacial Lakes
metas.note: The area of the Southern Alps, north and south of Queenstown, contains many glacial lakes, which can be recognized by their teal colours and clear waters.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Hawke’s Bay Hills
metas.note: Hawke’s Bay has dry, golden grassy hills, and in Generation 4 it will be sunny with a white Street View car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Marlborough Sounds
metas.note: The region of northern Marlborough, known as Marlborough Sounds, has densely forested mountains protruding from water.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Mount Egmont
metas.note: Mount Taranaki, often referred to as Mount Egmont, is easily distinguished due to its relatively smooth slopes and its pointed, often snowy peak. It can frequently be identified from afar, as the surrounding area is flat.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Mount Ruapehu
metas.note:
Coverage on Mount Ruapehu is easily identifiable due to the dark volcanic landscape and distinct lack of vegetation.

NOTE: This type of coverage is limited to the roads around the Whakapapa Ski Village.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Putauaki Volcano
metas.note: The volcano of Putauaki in eastern Bay of Plenty has a seemingly cut-off top which vaguely resembles the shape of a frog, with two big “eyes” protruding on either side of the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Sandy Cliffs
metas.note:
Bright sandy cliffs are a common sight in the central region of Manawatū-Whanganui. They may also be found in parts of Taranaki, Waikato and a road going into Hawke’s Bay.

NOTE: Sometimes the cliffs may appear like sandy rocks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Southern Alps
metas.note: The Southern Alps, a large, snowy mountain range, stretches throughout the majority of the South Island. Vegetation on the mountains becomes rarer the further south it is.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Tongariro National Park
metas.note: The area around Tongariro National Park is identifiable due to the low-lying volcanic vegetation in the area. Mount Ruapehu and Mount Tongariro are in the vicinity, and their tops are often covered by clouds.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - West Coast
metas.note: The West Coast and part of the Tasman region on the South Island can be recognized by its temperate rainforests and rugged landscape. This can be seen through the hundreds of tall hills and mountains, as well as the dark, compact greenery which is due to the area’s high level of rainfall.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Nigeria - Benue
metas.note: Benue state can be recognized by the lush, green grass covered ground, with reddish soil. The vegetation is somewhat scattered, with the grass making way for taller trees. Shorter trees and shrubs between the grass and taller trees are somewhat uncommon. Thatched huts are also common in comparison to other southern states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - Eastern Hilly Savannah
metas.note:
A savannah landscape combined with rocky hills can most commonly be seen in the northeast in the states of Plateau, Bauchi, Gombe, Adamawa, and the north of Taraba. The hills in the far east and west of this region are typically greener and covered in more vegetation compared to the hills toward the middle of the range.

NOTE: Around the city of Gombe, hills composed of softer, clay-like soil can be seen instead.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - Kano
metas.note: If you find yourself in an arid, but green, agricultural landscape with an abundance of corn around, you are likely to be in Kano state. It is only covered by shitcam, without any Generation 3 or 4.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - Lekki
metas.note: A flat landscape with coastal vegetation and many palms can be seen east of Lekki. The ground is very sandy. Almost all of the coverage is old Generation 3, with a silver follow car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - Niger
metas.note: Niger state is the shitcam equivalent to Benue state. It is almost entirely covered by shitcam, and can be recognized by the scattered trees, reddish soil, and dry grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - Northwest Arid Landscape
metas.note: The highways that run through the northwestern states of Kebbi, Sokoto, Zamfara, and Katsina can be recognized by an even more open and arid landscape compared to Niger state. The tree coverage becomes even more sparse, or there may not be trees at all. These states are entirely covered by shitcam.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Norway - Barren Highlands
metas.note: Barren highlands, with no trees or bushes, and often with rocky mountains along the road, are mostly found in the southwest.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Deep Fjords
metas.note: While fjords can be found along most of the Norwegian coast, deep fjords surrounded by tall mountains are most common between Bergen and Trondheim.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Far North Grassland
metas.note: Coastal grasslands with little to no other vegetation and only somewhat low, distant mountains can be found by coastal roads in the far north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Farmlands
metas.note: Large farmlands are mainly found in three areas, the southeast, the area surrounding Trondheim, and south of Stavanger.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Farmlands Trondheim
metas.note: The farmlands surrounding Trondheim are generally very hilly which are often quite steep
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Lofoten
metas.note: Distinct, sharp, rocky mountains with few trees can be seen on the Lofoten Archipelago.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Northeast Rolling Hills
metas.note: The northeast of Norway can typically be recognized by a somewhat rolling landscape, rather than tall mountains, and vegetation mainly consisting of very small birches combined with patched grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Russia Border
metas.note: Along the Russian border you can see this noticeably humid and green-looking road, with very overcast and occasionally foggy coverage. The trees are somewhat low and mainly consist of thin birches and pines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Oman - Bidiyah Shrubby Desert
metas.note: Sandy desert with light coloured green and yellow shrubs can be found in northeastern Oman, mainly south and west of Bidiyah.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Eastern Mountain Range
metas.note: Northern Oman features a dry mountainous landscape similar to eastern UAE. The south coast of Oman also rarely features some similar mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Fasad Dunes
metas.note:
A road going through large orange-pink sand dunes can be found north of Fasad.

NOTE: The same dunes can be seen in the distance close to the northern part of the Yemen border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Masirah Island
metas.note: Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. Road 51, which circulates the island, usually only has a white centre road line, which can help in recognising it. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Salalah Hills
metas.note: Close to the southern coast, especially around Salalah, you will find a rolling hills landscape. The area commonly features rocky ground, bushes and small trees as well as some fairly green valleys.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Oman - Ubar Fields
metas.note: Around the town of Ubar, you can find patches of green agricultural land surrounded by desert.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Panama - Aguadulce Fields
metas.note: The region around Aguadulce is relatively flat and features a lot of agricultural fields along with very brown or orange soil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Panama - David Fields
metas.note: The area around David is very flat, with lots of fairly open fields. Usually, mountains will be visible to the north and northeast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Panama - Tropical Rainforest
metas.note: Green tropical landscapes with palm trees and very tall grass are common around Colón and Panama City.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Panama - Volcán Landscape
metas.note: A mountainous landscape with pine trees, volcanic rocks, dry grass, and gravel roads can be found northeast of Volcán.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Peru - Agricultural Valleys
metas.note:
Coastal agricultural valleys in the middle and south are commonly sandwiched between dry mountains with no vegetation. The general orientation of these valleys are southwest-northeast.

NOTE: Agricultural valleys in the north of Peru can look similar, but often feature more shrubs and trees on the mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Exposed Rock
metas.note:
