In higher elevation areas near the centre of the country, exposed rocky outcroppings are commonly seen in the sides of hills and mountains. Some areas with the highest concentrations are near Lago Chinchaycocha (Junin District) stretching south towards the city of Ayacucho.

NOTE: Exposed rocks can rarely be seen anywhere in the country, so use this meta with some caution.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Flat Desert
metas.note: Areas near the cities of Ica, Arequipa, and Tacna feature barren and mostly flat desert landscapes that can resemble areas of northern Chile. You can typically see mountains in the distance, primarily while looking to the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Flat Valleys
metas.note:
A flat landscape in the mountains of Peru is usually seen in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.

NOTE: This landscape might look similar to Bolivia. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Huancayo Valley
metas.note: The valley connecting the cities of Jauja and Huancayo features a flat plain with plentiful trees, agricultural areas, and small villages. North-south oriented mountains can be seen on both edges of the valley.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Lake Chinchaycocha
metas.note: North of the city of Huancayo lies a shallow lake called Lake Chinchaycocha (also referred to as ‘the middle lake.’). This lake is generally marshy and a range of mountains can be seen to the east of the lake. This lake can look similar to Lake Titicaca, but is generally less densely populated and features fewer trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - North Piura Landscape
metas.note: Northwest of the city of Piura lies an area with similar vegetation to the area mentioned previously. However, this area is noticeably hillier.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Northern Lake Titicaca
metas.note: The coverage on the north side of Lake Titicaca was taken during a significantly wetter season than the coverage taken on the south side of Lake Titicaca.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Northern Mountains
metas.note: Far north Peru features mountains that are often covered in shrubby trees and bushes. Closer to the coast and the Ecuador border, these mountains are often quite dry in appearance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - South Piura Landscape
metas.note: The southwestern landscape of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is mostly flat, but you will sometimes see rolling hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Southern Lake Titicaca
metas.note: Low grass, a few hills, stone walls in villages and brown brick buildings are typical for the region south of Lake Titicaca in eastern Peru.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Tall Rocky Mountains
metas.note: Similarly, taller mountains near the middle of the country often feature rocky and sharp mountain tops. The main region of these mountains stretches from near the city of Huaraz southward to the city of Cusco; generally away from the coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Tarapoto Mountains
metas.note: The areas adjacent to the northern Amazonian city of Tarapoto feature moderately tall foliage-covered mountains and can bear a similar resemblance to the hilly areas of Colombia or Brazil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Tumbes
metas.note:
These three landscapes are typically found along offroads in Tumbes. You will always see sandy soil with either green or withered bushes.

NOTE: In addition, Tumbes does not have black cars on off roads. Make sure to consider it whenever you see such landscapes with a white Street View car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Volcanoes
metas.note:
Volcanoes are often seen in and around the city of Arequipa.

NOTE: Within Peru, volcanoes are only found in the southeast in the highlighted area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Philippines - Arayat Volcano
metas.note: The Arayat Volcano can be recognised by being completely surrounded by flat agricultural fields.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/philippines.

metas.name: Philippines - Bohol Hills
metas.note: On central Bohol you can find these distinct round grassy hills. The hills generally have dark brown soil beneath the grass, earning them the name of Chocolate Hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/philippines.

metas.name: Philippines - Mayon Volcano
metas.note: The Mayon Volcano is one of the tallest mountains in the Philippines and can be recognised by its almost perfect smooth cone shape. Beware that it will very often be covered in clouds.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/philippines.

metas.name: Philippines - Northern Luzon
metas.note: The forested mountain range in Northern Luzon is characterised by somewhat dry mountainsides and an abundance of pine trees. You may rarely come across a similar landscape on high-altitude roads in Mindanao.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/philippines.

metas.name: Portugal - Azores
metas.note: Most of the Azores visible on Street View consists of open agricultural fields in a rolling landscape, often with taller round hills in the background.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Portugal - Madeira
metas.note: Madeira is a very mountainous and semi-tropical island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Portugal - Serra da Estrela Natural Park
metas.note: The Serra da Estrela natural park can be recognised by the rocky mountainous highland landscape, often combined with yellow and black striped snow poles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Portugal - Southwest Flatland
metas.note: In the far southwest of the country you can find a flat uncultivated landscape with very limited vegetation, which typically appears quite dry. There are almost no trees nearby, and only very low bushes and grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Puerto Rico - Coast
metas.note: The North and South coasts of Puerto Rico typically feature flat coastal plains or rolling hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/puerto-rico.

metas.name: Puerto Rico - Mountains
metas.note: Most of the mountainous regions of Puerto Rico are located in the middle section of the country. Most of the coverage in these areas is limited to divided highways.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/puerto-rico.

metas.name: Puerto Rico - Southern Dryness
metas.note: Southern Puerto Rico can often look distinctly dryer than the rest of the island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/puerto-rico.

metas.name: Qatar - General Landscape
metas.note: Qatar's landscape is predominantly desert, with arid, and mostly flat expanses of sand as far as the eye can see. You will often not see a lot of trees or other greenery.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/qatar.

metas.name: Russia - Altai Mountains
metas.note: The main road of Altai Republic has a black car long antenna driving north through the Altai Mountains, often with foggy or rainy coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Buryatia
metas.note: The landscape in Buryatia is very unique, containing open grassy landscape with shrubs and mountains. It is lusher near Baikal, but the mountains persist.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Caspian Sea Area
metas.note: The area west of the Caspian Sea can often be recognised by its extremely dry and flat landscape, especially in Kalmykia, Astrakhan Oblast, and Dagestan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Caspian Sea Desert
metas.note: In the desert-like region west of the Caspian Sea, this completely flat and rural Generation 4 coverage on small poorly-tracked dirt roads can only be found in northern Dagestan and southwestern Astrakhan Oblast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Caucasus Mountains
metas.note: The Caucasus mountain range is one of the largest mountain ranges in Russia. The tallest mountain in Russia, Mount Elbrus, can be found on the border of the Kabardino-Balkarian Republic and Karachay-Cherkessia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Dagestan Fields
metas.note: Grassy fields, with bushy vegetation, in early spring Generation 4 coverage is typical for Dagestan. The landscape can either be completely flat or mountainous.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Far North
metas.note: The landscape in the far north can be recognised by the relatively flat landscape, with very low vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Kamchatka
metas.note: The Kamchatka peninsula has unique grey gravelly soil, as well as the largest number of volcanoes of any region in Russia. They are frequently seen across the peninsula, and in some places can appear quite close such as in Klyuchi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Kolyma Highway
metas.note: The eastern half of the Kolyma Highway going to Magadan features a lot of tall hills and mountains, usually shrouded in a haze. Most of the roads are unpaved and feature dark gravelly soil. The haze is not present in the western half.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Murmansk Area
metas.note: An open, hilly landscape with low shrubbery and fireweed usually indicates Murmansk. The lower the shrubbery, the more north it generally is.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Olkhon Island
metas.note: Olkhon Island on Lake Baikal has a single road, driving on rolling sandy hills during sunset. You can often see Lake Baikal directly with a mountain ridge across the bay.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Omsk
metas.note: The coverage in Omsk Oblast is some of the most recognizable in Russia. It is typically summer Generation 4 and has a distinct landscape consisting of green agricultural fields, which are interrupted by isolated patches of (primarily) birch forest. Note that in Generation 3, this landscape can be seen in a much larger area of Russia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Tunkinsky National Park
metas.note: Tunkinsky National Park in western Buryatia is a very green river basin with tall, jagged mountains to the north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Tuva Steppe Mountains
metas.note: Dry steppe mountains with a long antenna will usually indicate the Tuva Republic.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Vladivostok Area
metas.note: Lush and diverse forests in a hilly landscape characterises the noticeably warmer region around Vladivostok. Most of the coverage is overcast and has a white car with a long antenna. Further south, near the tri-border, you will find a more open rolling hill landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Rwanda - Akagera National Park
metas.note: The Akagera national park features a very vegetated yet dry landscape with wide unpaved roads that are reddish-brown in colour. You can also find these rectangular waystones at intersections. This coverage was taken with the brown Google car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: Rwanda - Northeastern Grassland
metas.note: Northeastern Rwanda has less extreme elevation compared to the rest of Rwanda. It more so consists of rolling hills and open agricultural land or undeveloped grassland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: Rwanda - Volcanoes
metas.note: Volcanoes and volcanic rocks can be seen in northwestern Rwanda.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: Senegal - Diourbel
metas.note:
Diourbel Region is the only region in Senegal with extensive rural coverage. The coverage in the region will look like this, with the Google Car driving on a sandy road with sparse trees. Some of the coverage extends to the west in the Thies region up to Babou.

NOTE: The sand in the coverage around Touba tends to be more grassy.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Eastern Dry Hills
metas.note: A dry landscape with slight hills can mostly be seen around Bakel, but also south to Nayé.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - North
metas.note: The landscape north of The Gambia and for Senegal generally is a flat, arid, savannah-desert landscape with sparse trees. The trees themselves will be somewhat short and have leaves that are faded in colour.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Rolling Coast
metas.note: A very slightly rolling landscape consisting of vegetated sand dunes can be seen along the northwestern coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - South
metas.note:
The vegetation in the region south of The Gambia is more lush and green compared to the rest of Senegal, and palm trees can be seen closer to the coast.

NOTE: Coverage toward the west will also be especially tropical. In addition, make sure not to confuse the south with some coverage near Dakar, which can look deceivingly green. However, here the vegetation will look a lot more low and coastal.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Southeast Green Hills
metas.note: A greener landscape with larger hills can be seen around Kedougou and Mako.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Serbia - Mountains
metas.note: A lush, green, mountainous landscape can be seen in the south and southeast, along the Bulgarian and Kosovo border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/serbia.

metas.name: Serbia - Northern Plains
metas.note: Vojvodina, the northern region between the Hungarian border and Belgrade, can be recognized by the flat, agricultural landscape. The landscape will be completely flat with no hills whatsoever.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/serbia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Mountains
metas.note:
Two wide valleys surrounded by tall, often sharp mountains can be found in the northern parts of the country.

NOTE: The light red area has tall, sharp mountains to the northwest, and much lower hills and mountains to the southeast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovenia - Mountains
metas.note: The tallest mountains in the country can be found in the northwestern alpine region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovenia.

metas.name: South Africa - Kruger National Park
metas.note:
The landscape around Kruger National Park is generally flat, with a savannah climate and dry vegetation. You will not see any agriculture and the vegetation is mostly made up of grasses, with small trees dotting the landscape. Red soil can also be seen below the grass. In addition, this distinctive directional waystone is commonly found at many junctions.

NOTE: Within the coverage of the park, you will mostly find unpaved gravel roads or small and paved roads without road lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Africa - Mozambique Border Flatness
metas.note: The landscape near the Mozambique border in the highlighted area is noticeably flat, with green subtropical vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Africa - Northeast
metas.note:
The northeast of the country can look very dry and somewhat barren, with a lot of orange or red soil. You will often see hills or mountains covered in shrubs.

NOTE: Depending on the season, the coverage can change drastically from dry to very green.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Africa - Northern Cape Dryness
metas.note:
A dry landscape with red soil is typically found in the Northern Cape.

NOTE: This map is a useful guide in guessing based on the climate of South Africa.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Africa - Rocky Mountains
metas.note:
Unique rocky, treeless mountains can be seen in Western Cape, with most of the mountains having tall, steep sides and sharp peaks.

NOTE: Similar mountains can be seen in and around Lesotho.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Africa - Western Cape Rolling Hills
metas.note: Grassy rolling hills are generally located in the coastal area of Western Cape between Cape Town and George, and just north of Cape Town. Tall ridges are usually visible to the north or east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Korea - General Landscape
metas.note: The South Korean landscape is predominantly mountainous. It is very rare to not see at least some hills or mountains in the distance. Even in the flat areas, you can almost always see elevation on the horizon.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-korea.

metas.name: South Korea - Gimje Plain
metas.note: The area around Gimje can be recognised by being one of the only completely flat areas of South Korea, combined with the open, yellow-green fields along almost every road in the area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-korea.

metas.name: South Korea - Jeju
metas.note: Jeju is a volcanic island with a lot of dark volcanic dirt, where you can also often see volcanoes in the distance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-korea.

metas.name: Spain - Aragon Dryness
metas.note: Very arid looking and mostly flat areas are common in central and south Aragón. The soil is very white and rocky in the northern part. Red soil is more common in Teruel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Castilla La Mancha
metas.note: Castilla la Mancha can have completely flat landscapes. Half of Spain’s wine is produced in this region, so vineyards are fairly common. In the western provinces of Ciudad Real and Toledo, it is very common to see olive tree plantations, generally in flatter ground than those found in Andalusia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - CastillaYLeon
metas.note: The centre of Castilla y León features a mostly flat agricultural landscape, with only slight changes in elevation. Most of the fields will have cereal crops like wheat and barley, and it is fairly common to find sunflower plantations.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Ebro Delta
metas.note: The Ebro delta (Deltebre in catalan) features an extremely flat landscape, where rice fields and water canals are very common. There are significant mountains to the South, West, and North, and some of them can be seen from almost every location in the delta.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Formentera
metas.note: The small island of Formentera frequently features low coastal shrubs. It is common to be able to see the mountains of Ibiza from Formentera’s north coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Fuerteventura
metas.note: The island of Fuerteventura in the Canary Islands is characterised by a very arid landscape with little to no vegetation. Orange soil is very common, and within the Canary Islands archipelago essentially unique to this island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Lanzarote Volcanic Rock
metas.note:
In some parts of the island of Lanzarote on the Canary Islands, a very dark, exposed volcanic soil can be seen. In places, this landscape superficially resembles the surface of the moon.

NOTE: The other Canary Islands can sometimes have similar landscapes as well, but it is by far the most common on Lanzarote.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Navarra Semi Desert
metas.note: Starting in Navarra and cutting across the middle of Aragón, there is a strip of semi-desert landscape on both sides of the Ebro river basin. Light sandy soil and small shrubs growing on small hills are common in this area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Northeast
metas.note: The landscape in the far north is much more green and lush than the rest of Spain. The landscape is generally quite hilly. Hedges and green meadows are common. In some places, this region’s landscape bears a vague resemblance to Ireland, France and the UK.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Pyrenees
metas.note:
The Pyrenees is a large mountain range on the border between Spain and France. Its mountains are some of the highest in all of Spain. It can be recognized by its light grey rock and abundance of pine trees. Local architecture features many rock walls.

NOTE: Andorra and the Spanish part of the Pyrenees look very similar in terms of landscape and architecture. And consider that the exclave of Llívia is part of Spain.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Sierra Nevada National Park
metas.note: The mountain range of Sierra Nevada features snowy peaks through the months of November and May. Sierra Nevada is the only mountain range in south Spain with snow during most of the year.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Drier Climate
metas.note:
Conversely, the rest of the country has a slightly more dry climate. The vegetation is often lower and more open. The landscape usually has a mix of brown and green tones.

Note that the difference is not extreme, as the landscape in Sri Lanka never truly gets downright arid.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Horton Plains National Park
metas.note: Horton Plains National Park has a very distinct and bait landscape, consisting of hilly plains covered in long grass. In the distance, you can see forests, but most of the park’s roads meander through a wide open landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Southern Climate
metas.note: The southwest of Sri Lanka has a more wet climate that is characterised by lush, dense vegetation. Deep green tones dominate the landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka.

metas.name: Sweden - Far North
metas.note: This type of vegetation, consisting of thin, weak-looking boreal trees and somewhat sandy soil can be found in the far north of Sweden.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Sweden - Mountains
metas.note: While it is possible to see forested mountains in several regions in the country, mountains with no trees at the top can only be found in the northwestern parts of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Sweden - Skåne
metas.note: In Skåne you will find the most open agricultural landscape in Sweden. It is the only region where, rather than a dense forest in the distance, you can get only a few small patches of trees strewn across the fields. On top of that, crops are often more diverse than the cereal crops, which are typical for the rest of Sweden.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Taiwan - Green and Orchid Island
metas.note:
The islands east of Taitung, Green Island and Orchid Island, are distinct due to the more tropical climate, abundance of coconut palms, and lush cliffs. Additionally, it is common to find run-down, concrete pavement.

NOTE: While the landscape between Green Island and Orchid Island are quite similar, a good way to distinguish the two is that Green Island frequently uses yellow outer lines. Additionally, Green Island is slightly more built-up.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Taiwan - Hsinchu Hills
metas.note: Miaoli and Hsinchu share a landscape of low rolling hills and winding roads as well as sparse farmland with vegetation that can look messy and unkempt.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Taiwan - Hualien
metas.note:
This open landscape with forests of short trees surrounding a narrow grassy road can be found in Hualien in the flat parts of Guangfu and Fenglin.

This area can be distinguished due to it being commonly covered in Generation 2; however, you can find similar landscapes in Generation 3 and 4.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Taiwan - Hualien Taitung Valley
metas.note:
The Hualien-Taitung Valley is a thin and long valley located on the east coast of the island passing from Hualien City at the north to Taitung City at the south. It is very recognizable as it consists of flat gentle plains surrounded by densely-forested mountains to the east and west.

NOTE: Most of the coverage on the east coast lies within this valley. There are also other valleys in central Taiwan that can look similar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Taiwan - Mountains
metas.note: The central-eastern region that covers two-thirds of Taiwan consists of forested mountains. The central mountain range that runs all the way to the south of the island is made up of tall mountains and rugged valleys. At high elevations, the vegetation can look less tropical and feature temperate or even coniferous trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Taiwan - Taichung Plains
metas.note: Similarly, Taichung features these open plains surrounded by low mountains that are often in the distance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Taiwan - Western Plains
metas.note: The central western plain of Taiwan mainly consists of flat to low rolling plains. It is common to find crops and other farmland in this area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Taiwan - Yilan Plain
metas.note:
The Yilan Plain is easily identifiable by the mountain ranges that are seen in the north, west, and south. Rice paddies are also extremely common as well as houses built right next to these fields.

NOTE: While the landscape on the surface can look quite similar to the valleys of Hualien and Taitung, unlike those two, you will almost never find mountains to the east in the plains of Yilan. Furthermore, the flat plains of Yilan are also generally more open.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Thailand - Chaiyaphum
metas.note: Chaiyaphum features very long and flat mountain ridges that can be seen from nearly anywhere in the province.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Doi Luang Chiang Dao
metas.note: Doi Luang Chiang Dao is the 3rd tallest mountain in Thailand. It along with other distinctly shaped mountains can be seen clearly from the Chiang Dao district of Chiang Mai.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Dry Flatland
metas.note:
Thailand has two regions that are relatively flat and dry compared to other areas. One north of Bangkok, the other more east.

NOTE: The eastern area feels sometimes a bit drier than the area north of Bangkok.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park
metas.note: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park in western Prachuap Khiri Khan features large, distinct exposed rock mountain massifs. Notably, the mountains can be seen from the center of the province.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Khao Sok National Park
metas.note: Khao Sok National Park in northern Phang-nga and western Surat Thani features some of the tallest and steepest exposed rock mountains in the south of Thailand. The mountains generally run east-west.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Krabi Rocks
metas.note: Western Krabi and parts of eastern Phang-nga also feature large exposed rock mountains running north-south.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Lopburi Mountains
metas.note: These distinctly shaped mountains can be found in southwestern Lopburi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Mukdahan
metas.note: The province of Mukdahan features many long, low hills among fields of rice, sugarcane, cassava and rubber trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Nakhon Vibes
metas.note: Brown paved roads among fields of sugarcane, cassava, and corn can be found in southeastern Nakhon Ratchasima.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - North Saraburi Mountains
metas.note: The northern half of Saraburi consists of large, exposed rock mountains in an east-west orientation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Phetchabun Valley
metas.note: Large north-south mountains can be seen on either side of the Phetchabun valley.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Phrao Valley
metas.note: The Phrao District in Chiang Mai is a fairly flat valley surrounded by mountains in all directions. The valley will commonly grow rice and fruit.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Rocky Mountains
metas.note: Steep mountains with a lot of exposed rock are most commonly found in the west and on the peninsula.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Smooth Mountains
metas.note: Low, smooth and forested mountains can be found in the centre-north of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Tak Hills
metas.note: Rolling hills of corn or sugar cane fields can be found in the west of the Tak province. In this area, paved roads are often very brown.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Thailand - Tall Mountains
metas.note:
Tall mountains are most often seen in northwestern Thailand.

NOTE: Some parts of the southern peninsular part are also mountainous.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Tunisia - Central Region
metas.note: The large middle region between Hammamet and Gabes is very flat, and more arid. Olive tree plantations are common and the more south you go, the drier the landscape becomes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Tunisia - Gabes Desert
metas.note: South of Gabes is where the landscape changes into something more akin to a desert. A lot more rubbish and small white rocks can be found along the roads. Olive tree plantations are still somewhat common. A mountain range far in the distance is often visible to the southwest.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Tunisia - Hammamet Hills
metas.note: The area between Tunis and Hammamet looks similar to the area north of Tunis, but the hills tend to be higher and more vegetated.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Tunisia - Lake Bizerte
metas.note: Bizerte Lake is instantly recognizable due to its teal coloured waters. There are slight hills to its south, with the rest of the area around the lake being flat. The city of Bizerte is located on the northeast side of the lake.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Tunisia - North
metas.note: The area north of Tunis has a Mediterranean climate with hilly terrain. The region is very agricultural and at the time the coverage was captured, almost all fields laid fallow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Turkey - Far East Grassland
metas.note: In the northeast you will find uncultivated grasslands in valleys surrounded by round hills. Trees are very limited in the region. In Generation 3 the area has an extremely distinct look, with deep green grass covering the hills. It is significantly more difficult to recognise in Generation 4, where the grass has a more arid look.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Lake Van
metas.note: Lake Van is by far the biggest lake in Turkey and has a semi-arid landscape, being surrounded by dry grassy hills and occasional trees and agricultural fields near the shore.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Mount Ararat
metas.note: Mount Ararat, labelled as Ağrı Dağı on Google Maps, is a dormant volcano in far eastern Turkey and the tallest mountain in the country. It is often seen together with Küçük Ağrı, a smaller volcano to the southeast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - North
metas.note: Northern Turkey tends to be significantly lusher and more forested than the rest of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Steep Valleys
metas.note: River valleys surrounded by steep, barren and rocky cliff sides can be found between the cities of Erzurum and Artvin and in the southeast near the city of Hakkâri.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Uganda - Crater
metas.note:
On the northern coverage, it is common to see large, water-filled craters. Similar craters cannot be found elsewhere in the country.

The only paved road with coverage outside Kampala can be found here. The pavement almost entirely lacks the red tinge which is typical for most roads in the country. The road has white, solid outer lines and a yellow middle line.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uganda.

metas.name: Uganda - Kidepo National Park
metas.note: The National Park is located in the northeastern parts of the country and mostly consists of a large savannah with mountains being visible in most directions. The most recognizable mountain range can be seen to the east and is visible in most of the coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uganda.

metas.name: Uganda - Lake Mburo National Park
metas.note: The park is located west of lake Victoria and has by far the driest coverage in the country. The grass is almost always completely dried out, which is normally enough to recognise it. Bushes and trees along the road also typically look very dry. The area is quite hilly, but not mountainous.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uganda.

metas.name: Uganda - Murchison Falls National Park
metas.note: The National Park is located by the northern end of Lake Albert and can commonly be recognized by the low dirt barriers along the side of the roads. A savannah can be seen in the western part, while the eastern parts contain many small trees and bushes. Apart from a fairly low and wide mountain range far away to the west, there are no mountains in the vicinity.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uganda.

metas.name: Uganda - Queen Elizabeth National Park
metas.note: Queen Elizabeth National Park, north of Lake Edward, is one of the only places in Uganda where you will commonly see dirt which is not red. Instead, the dirt will typically be either brown or greyish.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uganda.

metas.name: Ukraine - Mountains
metas.note: The Carpathian Mountains is an area in western Ukraine that is significantly hillier than the rest of the country, in some places bordering on mountainous. It is also much more forested, with very little agriculture, and a lot of pine trees. The roads going through it tend to be more curvy, rather than the straight highways found in the rest of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: Ukraine - South Fields
metas.note: Towards the south, the climate becomes warm and dry. The landscape is rather arid. Larger Forests are quite rare and make way for shrubs and open fields.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gulf of Oman
metas.note: If you see mountains to the west, and flatness to the east, you are likely near the Gulf of Oman, in the extreme East of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Mountains
metas.note: Mountains are only found in the far east of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Northern Mountains
metas.note: You can easily recognise the Northern part of the emirate of Ras al Khaimah thanks to the light-coloured mountains visible to the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Lake District
metas.note: The Lake District is very hilly, with a lot of exposed rocks and stone walls. It can look like the Scottish Highlands, but Scotland is generally less rocky.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scotland Highlands
metas.note: The Scottish Highlands can be distinguished by the semi-barren, very mountainous landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United States - Appalachians
metas.note:
The Appalachian mountain range is a low mountain range that runs through the eastern states. The general landscape consists of low, forested mountains, with beech and oak trees being a common sight.

NOTE: Houses in the south generally have less storeys. New England architecture, commonly consisting of wood panelling, high roofs and a porch, is also more common toward the north, especially in New England.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Badlands National Park
metas.note: Badlands National Park features these distinct, sand-brown, eroded rock formations. The formations may sometimes appear more rounded, and lighter in colour.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Big Bend National Park
metas.note: Big Bend National Park is located along the Mexico border in Southwest Texas. It can be identified by its dry, rocky peaks and shrubby foliage. This park is adjacent to the Chihauhan desert, so plants such as yucca and prickly pear cactus are common. The roads in the national park are covered in Generation 3.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - California Central Valley
metas.note: Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here. In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Central Appalachians
metas.note: In the Appalachian area stretching from southern New York to southern Virginia, there are a lot of forest-covered rolling hills, with flat valleys dividing them. A majority of the ridges are oriented Southwest to Northeast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Central Colorado Ridge
metas.note: Central Colorado is home to a large North-to-South oriented mountain ridge. This divides the Rocky Mountains to the west and the Great Plains to the east. These mountains are adjacent to the major metropolitan areas of Boulder, Denver, and Colorado Springs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Coastal Maui
metas.note: Coastal areas of Maui are noticeably more lush and green. Banana plants, palm trees, and views of the mountains are all common.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Death Valley National Park
metas.note:
Death Valley National Park can be easily recognized by the dry, sandy, treeless mountains that can be seen from the roads that go through the park. In Generation 3 coverage, the sky can look particularly dusty.

NOTE: Many smaller roads in Death Valley only have Generation 1 coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Devils Tower
metas.note: In far Northeastern Wyoming lies Devil’s Tower, which is a very tall, standalone butte protruding from the surrounding land. This can sometimes be seen from many miles away because of the lack of nearby mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Florida Low Hills
metas.note: The area between the cities of Orlando and Lakeland in Florida sometimes feature low, rolling hills. Lakes and agricultural fields are also common in this area. This is the only main hilly area in central or southern Florida.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Great Basin
metas.note: The Great Basin, centred around Nevada, can be recognized by the tall, sometimes snow-capped mountains in the background. There are dry, but grassy, and slightly shrubby plains leading up to the mountains. The tallest mountains are in Nevada, Utah and California. More gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon, and greener mountains can be seen in Idaho and central Utah.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Great Plains
metas.note: The Great Plains are in the middle of the United States and stretch from the Canadian border in the North, to central Texas in the South. This area is primarily flat with few trees. Some areas feature agriculture fields, while others feature dry and barren grassy fields.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Guadalupe Mountains
metas.note: Along the New Mexico and or Texas border there is a ridge of tall, dry peaks known as the Guadalupe Mountains. In adjacent areas of both states, smaller foothills of these mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Guam North
metas.note: Similarly, the northern half of the island is mostly flat.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Guam South
metas.note: Hills are mostly found on the southern half of the island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Hawai’i Plains
metas.note: The Island of Hawai’i (also referred to as The Big Island) is both the largest and farthest southeast island with Street View coverage in the state. The interior areas feature rolling, grassy plains and volcanic rocks. You can typically see one or more of the island’s volcanoes from the road. Both Generation 3 and Generation 4 coverage are common in this area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Hawaiʻi Forests
metas.note:
Rural roads going through forests within a flat landscape are commonly found south of the city of Hilo, on the island of Hawaiʻi.

NOTE: Mountainous forests are dotted around Hawaii, but if you are in one, and you see red soil with Generation 3, consider guessing in Kauai, the westernmost covered island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Hawaii Red Hill
metas.note: The Red Hill can easily be recognised by this unique barren, red rocky landscape. Due to the high altitude, clouds are usually visible below you.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Hawaiian Lattice
metas.note: The infamous “Hawaiian lattice” can be recognized by the volcanic soil and rocks that are abundant in the region. Volcanic vegetation can also be seen lining the roads. Note that the angle of the roads is a big clue for the area, and that this lattice was built on the slope of Mauna Loa.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Kauai Landscape
metas.note:
The Island of Kauai is the furthest west island in Hawaii with official Google coverage. This island has deep red soil and has large rugged hills with lush, jungle-like vegetation. This island also has exclusively Generation 3 coverage.

NOTE: Other islands such as Maui and Molokaʻi have similar soil colours, but the hillsides on them will typically have less dense vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Lānaʻi Central Region
metas.note: The Island of Lānaʻi is a small, yet distinct island that lies just south of Moloka’i. A volcano is found just east of the centre of the island, adjacent to the town of Lānaʻi. In this area, tall Cook pines are abundant. In addition, some main roads near the centre of the island are lined with younger Cook pines. The island only has Generation 3 coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Lānaʻi Coastal Hills
metas.note: Towards the coasts of the island of Lānaʻi, hills dotted with dry grass and shrubby vegetation are commonly seen. These areas are very rural with few buildings.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Lower Mississippi River Valley
metas.note: The Lower Mississippi River Valley is a very flat and open landscape with red soil in areas of Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi, and Northeast Louisiana. Corn and other crops are common in this area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Maui Plains
metas.note: The Island of Maui sits southeast of Molokaʻi. In the centre of the island, you will find dry and somewhat flat grasslands with one or both of the mountain ranges on the island visible. Both Generation 3 and Generation 4 coverage are common on the island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Mesa Landscape
metas.note: The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Molokaʻi Landscape
metas.note: The Island of Molokaʻi is just southeast of the Island of Oʻahu. This island features deep red soil, dry-looking vegetation, and a prominent volcano on the eastern end of the island. Molokaʻi is also very sparsely populated. This island only has Generation 3 coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Nebraska Sandhills
metas.note: The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Ouachita Mountains
metas.note: The Ouachita Mountains stretch from Eastern Oklahoma into West-Central Arkansas. Unlike the nearby Ozark Mountains, these mountains are typically more steep in nature and easier to see from a distance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Prairie Potholes
metas.note: The area spanning from the Montana Border with Saskatchewan to the Western Great Lakes features many ‘prairie potholes.’ These are areas of low-lying wetlands that feature marshy grasses and small, shallow ponds.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Rio Grande Valley
metas.note: The Rio Grande Valley in South Texas is extremely flat and features shrubby trees and agricultural fields. This area borders the Mexican state of Tamaulipas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Rocky Mountains
metas.note: The area stretching from the Canadian border to Northern New Mexico is home to the Rocky Mountains. These jagged, rocky formations often feature many pine trees and visible snow all-year round at the highest peaks. Some areas of the Rocky Mountain Range are noticeably dry, with few trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - San Antonio Hills
metas.note: Just west of the metropolitan areas of Austin and San Antonio Texas lies a large area of dry, rocky hills featuring many yucca and prickly pear plants. Texas Live Oak trees are the predominant tree type in this area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - South Florida Jungle
metas.note: Deep South Florida, between the metropolitan areas of Ft. Myers and Miami, features dense, jungle-like forests that have few inhabitants. Roads through these areas are commonly very straight and long.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Theodore Roosevelt National Park
metas.note:
Theodore Roosevelt National Park features similar, sand-brown, eroded rock formations to Badlands National Park. The rock formations in this park tend to have more trees on them. Additionally, almost all coverage has fall colours visible.

NOTE: Similar formations can be seen in far eastern Montana as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Tundra
metas.note: Most of interior and northern Alaska lies in subarctic or tundra climate zones. These areas feature relatively low amounts of forest undergrowth and shorter trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Washington Golden Fields
metas.note:
Agricultural golden fields can commonly be seen in eastern Washington.

NOTE: Flat areas of northern and eastern Oregon can have a similar appearance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - West Coast Rainforests
metas.note:
Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.

NOTE: These rainforests stretch north into coastal British Columbia and Southeast Alaska as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - West Oklahoma Peaks
metas.note: Southwestern Oklahoma features a small area of rocky, shrubby peaks. Some of the mountains are also covered in trees, and the rocks can have a pinkish red tint to them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: Uruguay - Eastern Flatland
metas.note: The region near Lagoa Mirim and the Brazil border in the southeast of the country is noticeably very flat, in contrast to the slight hills found in most of the rest of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.

metas.name: Uruguay - General Landscape
metas.note: This is the stereotypical Uruguay round. The coverage often, but not always, features overcast weather. Most of the landscape consists of open grasslands with gentle hills. Occasionally, you might see separated tree plantations. Roads are generally in worse condition than in neighbouring countries.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.

metas.name: Uruguay - Minas Hills
metas.note:
The landscape near the town of Minas is recognizable: some of the tallest hills in the country, with lots of exposed rocks, and often heavy bushland vegetation. The image shown here is a fairly extreme example of this landscape – usually it is more subtle. However, the exposed rock is always a good clue.

NOTE: The landscape in the Quebrada de los Cuervos nature reserve, situated further north, can look similar. In addition, there are also very tall hills in the north of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.

metas.name: Uruguay - Northern Hills
metas.note: You can also find tall hills in the north of the country. These can be recognized by their noticeably darker soil. These hills also typically do not have the exposed rocks that are visible in the Minas hills. The vegetation tends to be natural, and you will often see tree plantations. This specific landscape tends to be most noticeable very close to the Brazil border, on Route 30 near Tranqueras.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.
